register.text: Korea Treasury Bonds sold by competitive auction each month, which fund the government budget as a whole; no one of the seven standards is named. Since April 2026 fixed-rate bonds in won have been phased into the FTSE World Government Bond Index, where they are to make up 1.75% of the index once fully included.

register.name: Social covered bond, Korea Housing Finance Corporation
register.detail: Korea Housing Finance Corporation · issued 1 September 2026 · matures 1 September 2029 · ISIN XS3465646365 · under a US$15bn covered bond programme
register.note: The Corporation has issued all its covered bonds and mortgage-backed securities as social bonds since March 2019
register.text: A three-year social covered bond of the Korea Housing Finance Corporation in euros, its latest issue. The social value the Corporation names for its bonds is housing welfare for low-to-moderate income households, which serves the shelter standard.

items.name: Happy Dosirak Social Cooperative
items.text: Korea’s first social cooperative, with 26 lunchbox centres across the country among its members, which provides public meal services and makes and delivers lunchboxes for children at risk of missing meals, as for 40 children in Gunpo under an agreement signed in April 2025.

items.name: Dot
items.text: A Korean company that makes the Dot Pad, a tactile display that turns braille text, images, charts and diagrams into touchable graphics, which schools for the blind in South Korea and other countries supply to their students.

items.name: Goodwill Store
items.text: A chain of 36 thrift shops across the country, set up in 2011 to hire people with autism and developmental disorders, which sells secondhand goods such as clothes and processed food and employs 451 people with developmental disorders.
